name: Ariva Phase 1: pilot MVP
description: Phase 1 (pilot MVP): the Border module at one AMAN arrivals hall, measured end to end, validated against manual counts, tracers and observer logs, and deployable single-tenant in the border authority's environment. Builds on Phase 0 (backlog/prd-phase0.json) and runs alongside the ASVS gap stories (backlog/prd-asvs-gaps.json, not duplicated here). Priorities 1 to 31 need no site decision and can start before the pilot contract; stories from priority 30 carry 'Blocked on' notes. The dev cluster release (ARV-002's last criterion) is deferred by the owner (2026-10-06) to ARV-137, after every other MVP story; no Kubernetes cluster work is scheduled before it. AMAN-side outbox changes belong to the AMAN repository and are listed as dependencies only. Gate: pilot go-live (ARV-138), then pilot acceptance.

userStories.title: [E12] Per-line minute counts in the stream
userStories.description: Pilot count accuracy (F18) is judged per line and per 15-minute bin, but the stream stores entries and exits per queue zone only (queue_minute). Write per-line crossing counts per minute so validation and reports can compare each line with manual counts. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-89, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: A new versioned script creates the line_minute hypertable (zone key, line name, line role, minute, profile version, in, out, source) with the retention class of queue_minute; its SHA-256 is added to checksums.lock
Ariva.Api.Stream writes line_minute by binary COPY in the same checkpoint transaction as queue_minute; an integration test restarts mid-stream and gets identical rows (idempotent upsert)
Counts come from Ariva's own crossings; vendor line crossings (ariva.device.vendor-line-crossing.v1) are stored as a separate source for cross-check and never mixed into Ariva's counts
The golden replay covers line_minute; the existing output hash is unchanged or the new golden is recorded in backlog/progress.md with the reason
Unit tests: crossings on entry, exit, count and overflow entry lines land on their line and minute; late events inside the watermark revise the open minute only

userStories.title: [E12] Continuous health checks: conservation, track completion and occupancy sanity
userStories.description: The F18 continuous checks (conservation residual, track completion rate, occupancy between 0 and the zone's physical capacity) are not computed anywhere. Compute them per zone and 15-minute bin in the stream, store them with the bin, and serve them through an API. Zones get an optional physical capacity in draft profiles. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-120, CWE-863.
acceptanceCriteria: Queue and overflow zones of a draft profile accept an optional physical capacity (1 to 5,000 people); published versions stay immutable; the geometry hash rule (F22) is unchanged or its new version documented

Pure HealthChecks in Ariva.Core/Queueing compute per zone and bin: conservation residual (F18), track completion rate (tracks exited over tracks entered, with censored and still-open tracks reported apart) and minutes with occupancy outside 0 to capacity; table-driven tests from F18, including bins with no entries
A versioned script adds a zone_health_bin table (or columns on queue_bin, one row per bin revision) written by the stream with the bin; the golden replay reproduces it
GET api/v1/sites/{siteCode}/zone-health by zone and range with a new permission DataQuality.View in the role mapping and security/permission-matrix.json; [SiteScoped]; range capped
E2E: values for the reference evening, permission matrix rows, cross-site request returns 404 without data, oversized range 400

userStories.title: [E12] Overflow band occupancy, OverflowDetected and the OverflowOccupied rule
userStories.description: The engine already sums overflow bands into the queue length (Ariva.Core/Queueing/QueueInputs.cs), but the stream does not store a band's own occupancy, nothing produces ariva.flow.overflow-detected.v1, and the OverflowOccupied metric has no data (Ariva.Infra/Alerting/AlertInputs.cs), so seeded rule R-002 shows 'Not evaluated yet'. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-862.
acceptanceCriteria: The stream records each overflow band's occupancy per minute and overflow minutes per bin (Proposed definition: a minute with any occupancy, TC-19), in a versioned script, written in the checkpoint transaction
OverflowDetected is produced once when a band becomes occupied and once when it empties, keyed by site and queue zone, described in docs/architecture/asyncapi.yaml (the AsyncAPI test passes)
AlertInputs supplies OverflowOccupied; R-002 is evaluated live and in backtest, and a test proves backtest equals live on a scenario with an occupied band
Replays reproduce the overflow rows and events (golden replay updated with the reason if it changes)

userStories.title: [E12] Zone keys that fit the outbox: ZoneHealthChanged and every event keyed by zone
userStories.description: outbox_message.message_key is varchar(200) (script 0011), but a zone key <site>/<queue zone name> can reach 218 characters (a site of up to 17, a zone name of up to 200). ARV-115 made the stream drop an OverflowDetected whose key is too long and made the NHibernate outbox fail such a commit with the reason (OutboxLimits) instead of a database error 22001; the commit still fails, so ZoneHealthChanged (SvcDeviceHealth: the device health consumer and the periodic sweep) for such a zone fails on every attempt, and a sweep that assesses that zone never commits. Remove the cause rather than the symptom. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-120, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: A zone profile refuses a queue or overflow zone name whose zone key with the site's code would exceed OutboxLimits.MaxMessageKeyLength (200), with a clear validation message; existing published profiles are checked by a test or a migration note (none at DMO exceed it)
Or, if the owner prefers, message_key is widened by a new versioned script (never by editing 0011) and OutboxLimits follows it; the choice is recorded in docs/product/decisions.md
SvcDeviceHealth's sweep commits the other zones when one zone's event cannot be written (no zone blocks the sweep); integration test with a zone key over the limit
Unit tests for the profile rule; integration test that ZoneHealthChanged for the longest allowed key reaches the outbox

userStories.title: [E12] Staff and service zone occupancy into the desk engine
userStories.description: The MVP needs desk state from AMAN and from sensor zones. The stream drops non-queue zones, so Staff and Service zone readings never reach the DeskStateEngine (formulas F10 implementation note). Feed them at their F10 rank so desks without a live AMAN signal still get a state, and so the shadow nowcast (ARV-117) has a sensor-only desk term. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: Staff and Service zone occupancy readings of the published profile reach the site's desk engine as staff presence and service activity signals, matched to their desk through the profile; AMAN sessions keep their higher rank
desk_minute records sensor-derived seconds and the Degraded flag as F10 and F11 define; staleness turns silent sensor sources Unknown

The sensor emulator emits staff and service zone occupancy for the reference evening; a scenario test shows the engine's open desks from sensors alone match the scenario within one desk for at least 95 percent of minutes (Proposed bound, recorded)
Only counts cross from the zone processor to the desk engine; no track id reaches desk_minute (unit test)
Buffers stay bounded per desk and per engine under a flood of zone readings (unit test)

userStories.title: [E12] Sensor-only shadow nowcast for the ground-truth proof
userStories.description: The pilot's ground-truth proof is the nowcast error with and without AMAN inputs, side by side. The desk term is live only and never replayed (formulas F8), so the comparison cannot be rebuilt later. Compute and store, next to the published nowcast, a shadow nowcast that uses no AMAN input. It is never shown to staff, passengers or rules. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-862, CWE-863.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned script adds the shadow nowcast and its no-service reason to queue_minute; the stream writes both in the same row as the published nowcast

The shadow uses Nowcast.Compute without AMAN-derived inputs (AMAN sessions in n_open, AMAN cycle time, AMAN reject rate), with the sensor desk term from ARV-116 or the exit term alone; unit tests on the F8 cases show the two differ only through those inputs
The shadow value is not in the live snapshot, the hub, displays, alert inputs or reports (unit or architecture test); it is read only by the validation comparison (ARV-104f)

userStories.title: [E12] Sensor-only desk engine per site for the shadow nowcast
userStories.description: Owner decision 2026-10-07 (ARV-117): while AMAN's session is live the desk engine takes AMAN's rank, so desk_minute records no sensor-derived open time for a desk with an AMAN code, and at a site where every desk has one (AUH) the shadow nowcast is the exit term alone whenever AMAN is live. Add a second desk engine per site, fed only by the desks' staff and service zones (never AMAN sessions, statistics or transactions), so that desk_minute (or a parallel shadow desk table) records sensor-only open seconds even while AMAN is live. The shadow nowcast's desk term reads it, so at all-AMAN sites the pilot's ground-truth proof compares AMAN's desk term against the sensor desk term, not against the exit rate. Never shown to staff, passengers or rules. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-862, CWE-863, CWE-501, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: A sensor-only desk engine per site runs beside the published one in the desk feed of Ariva.Api.Stream, fed only by staff and service zone readings; a test shows that no AMAN session, statistic or transaction changes its output (CWE-501: every reading validated against its contract before use)

Its sensor-only open seconds per desk and minute are written in the same checkpoint transaction as the published desk minutes, either as columns of desk_minute or in a parallel shadow desk table from a versioned script (checks, runtime role without DELETE or TRUNCATE, SHA-256 in checksums.lock)

Bounded (CWE-120): desks per site, open desk minutes and readings held per engine are capped, with a counted warning that names the site and the count only; the engine's state is part of the desk feed snapshot, validated on restore (an invalid or oversized snapshot is refused and rebuilt by replay)

The shadow nowcast's desk term (ARV-117, DeskTerms.SensorOnly) reads the sensor-only open seconds; unit tests on the F8 cases show that at an all-AMAN site with AMAN live the shadow uses the sensor desk term (n_open from the zones), and that the published nowcast is unchanged
Replay is deterministic: the golden scenario (seed 9303) produces the same output hash every run; a changed hash is explained and recorded in backlog/progress.md

No new read path (CWE-862, CWE-863): the sensor-only desk values are not in the live snapshot, the hub, displays, alert inputs, reports or the AMAN contracts; ShadowNowcastExposureTests and the pg_depend integration test are extended to the new columns or table

userStories.title: [E12] Availability ledger per operating minute
userStories.description: Pilot criterion: availability 99 percent of operating hours. Nothing measures it. Define an available minute (Proposed: every published queue zone of the site has a live snapshot younger than the staleness threshold and a queue_minute row) and record one row per site and minute, with operating hours from a site calendar. Epic: Measurement completeness. CWEs to review: CWE-862, CWE-863, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: Site operating calendar (weekly hours in site local time plus dated exceptions and announced maintenance windows) with API under the site's edit permission, [SiteScoped], audited; maintenance windows count only when recorded before they start

A Cronz job (single leader, idempotent per site and minute) writes availability_minute with the reasons for an unavailable minute (stale zone, missing minute, stream lag); it reads Redis snapshots and the database only, no HTTP calls to other hosts
Availability per day, week and date range equals available operating minutes over operating minutes; unit tests with calendar edges, DST-free UTC storage and maintenance windows

userStories.title: [E20] Second seed site modelled on a real airport: AUH Terminal A arrivals (illustrative)
userStories.description: Owner request 2026-10-06: demo data modelled on a real airport besides the fictional DMO. Abu Dhabi Zayed International (AUH) Terminal A arrivals immigration hall, built only from public information; there is no real plan, and an illustrative sample is accepted. Cited public facts: Terminal A 742,000 m2 built-up area, 45 million passengers a year, 11,000 passengers an hour, 79 aircraft stands at a time, opened November 2023, X-shaped design by KPF (Gulf News, WAM, KPF); arrivals on the lower level with immigration, baggage claim and customs in a straight line, then landside transport (The National, BDC Network); 38 immigration counters and 34 smart gates reported by secondary travel guides (propertyfinder.ae, morafiq.ae, the airport's terminal guides; unverified, marked 'reported'); smart gates for UAE residents and eligible nationals, most first-time visitors at a staffed counter, biometric face and iris corridors since May 2026 (visahq news 2026-05-07). Everything else is an assumption. Epic: Demo data. CWEs to review: CWE-269, CWE-79, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: A second seed topology with site code AUH-TA (valid under the Site code rule): airport AUH, Terminal A, the lower arrivals level, the arrivals immigration checkpoint, 38 manual counters and 34 smart gates (both labelled 'reported'), queue zones with their lanes: citizens and residents with smart gates (CIT, RES, EG), GCC nationals (GCC), visitors and visa on arrival (VIS), crew and diplomatic (CRW, DIP), transfer (TRF, labelled an assumption since transfer flows normally bypass arrivals immigration), overflow bands, service and staff zones, devices with coverage, and a published zone profile

Every dimension, count, lane split and position that is not a cited public fact is marked as an assumption in the seed source and in its doc page (docs/demo/auh-terminal-a.md, which cites each public fact with its URL)

The site carries an 'Illustrative, not surveyed' flag set only by the seed; the web shell shows it as a persistent banner on every screen of that site and on its passenger displays; Playwright checks the banner in English and Arabic

Geometry sits on an illustrative floor plan image loaded through the existing floor plan upload and calibration (ARV-018, ARV-053); the doc page explains how to replace it with a real plan at runtime (a real plan, for example under NDA, is never committed)
Same guard as the DMO seed: refused outside vm-local, k8s-dev and k8s-demo (DemoSeedExtensions), idempotent, an integration test proves a re-run changes nothing and that both seeds coexist
No officer, traveller or document identifier and no real AUH staff or system names in the seed (data boundary test)
